note: موت centrally and overwhelmingly means death/demise. The source's 'urine, piss' is a separate vulgar/Indic homograph contamination and should not be mixed into this standard learner entry.
سمیت functions as a postposition/particle meaning including/together with. 'Closed-class' is too vague.
فی is a distributive postposition/particle meaning per/each. 'Closed-class' is too vague for learner grammar.
کارکردگی centrally means performance/functioning/output/efficiency. The generic gloss 'work' is too vague and misses 'performance'.
ہمیشہ is primarily the adverb always/forever. 'Eternal' is an adjectival English derivative rather than the normal direct use, so adjective POS is unnecessary.
آمدنی means income/earnings/revenue in modern Urdu. 'Arrival, coming' is confusion with آمد and should be removed.
ضرور means certainly/definitely/surely and often conveys necessarily/must in context. Interjection POS is not needed.
انتہائی can mean extreme/utmost adjectivally and very commonly functions as 'extremely'. Adjective-only POS misses that learner-important use.
اچھا centrally means good/nice/fine and also okay/well as an interjection/adverb. The source omits 'good' and includes the spurious noun gloss 'aim'.
proposed_english: good; nice; fine; well; okay; alright

note: پسند is the noun liking/preference/choice and can describe something liked/pleasing in compounds. The English verb-like gloss 'like' without grammatical framing is ambiguous.
کون is the interrogative pronoun 'who?', not a noun in ordinary use.
یوں means thus/like this/in this way/so. 'Actually' is not a normal direct meaning and should be removed.
proposed_english: thus; like this; in this way; so

note: ہدایت means guidance/instruction/direction and is also used as a personal name. 'The truth' is not a suitable core English gloss.
proposed_english: guidance; instruction; direction; Hidayat (personal name, context-dependent)
